summary: Ambiguous role-path normalization in cross-account broker causing intermittent AssumeRole failures for prod jobs
description: Issue summary: Several scheduled production jobs running in prod/us-east intermittently fail when the cross-account broker attempts to assume an AWS role on behalf of Redwood service runners. Impact: Several nightly data-sync and model-refresh jobs failed to start between 2026-03-11 22:00 and 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC. Failures are causing delayed model cache priming and increased tail latency for user requests. Scope appears limited to accounts that use hierarchical role paths (roles with a '/' in the name) and to some GCP->AWS federated flows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a job that uses the ops-broker to assume-role into customer-linked AWS account with role ARN containing nested path (e.g., arn:aws:iam::012345678901:role/teams/ops/service-runner)
2) Trigger an identity exchange via the federated broker (GCP Workload Identity Federation or SAML assertion path), using the broker's canonicalize step enabled
3) Observe broker logs and AWS STS response when calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or AssumeRoleWithSAML
4) Reproduce intermittently by toggling broker normalization setting (on/off) and running parallel assume requests to different roles with similar suffixes
observed_behavior: Broker logs show role lookup succeeds but the subsequent STS call returns AccessDenied or InvalidIdentityToken for some requests. Example error from logs: 'STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed for role arn:aws:iam::012345678901:role/teams/ops/service-runner - AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity'. Additional traces show the broker sometimes strips intermediate path components when resolving role ARNs, causing the wrong role name to be used in the STS call (e.g., resolved to role 'service-runner' instead of 'teams/ops/service-runner').
expected_behavior: Broker should preserve full role path when resolving ARNs and only attempt AssumeRole against the exact role ARN advertised in the mapping table. Federated identity tokens should be presented with the correct RoleSessionName and session tags so AWS accepts the assume request.
logs_and_artifacts: ops-broker log excerpt (2026-03-11T23:14:08Z): broker[auth] INFO resolving role mapping for principal: svc-account-324
AWS STS response (2026-03-11T23:14:09Z): Error: AccessDenied when calling AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: role ARN mismatch or unauthorized
GCP token debug (2026-03-11T23:14:07Z): audience/claims present; aud contains broker client ID; no token expiry anomalies
initial_triage_and_hypotheses: Hypothesis 1: A recent change to broker path-normalization introduced a bug that strips path segments when role names contain multiple slashes.
Hypothesis 2: Role resolution lookup in the mapping cache uses suffix-based matching which can return a shorter role name when multiple role ARNs share the same trailing segment.
Hypothesis 3: Some affected AWS accounts have org policies requiring exact path matching; the broker's canonicalized name violates that policy and causes AccessDenied
Hypothesis 4: GCP->AWS federation token attribute (e.g., role_session_name) missing due to header trimming in proxy, leading AWS to reject the assume request

resolution: Workaround: Disabled the 'canonicalize path segments' feature in the ops-broker on prod (rolled as a hotfix) which restored normal AssumeRole behavior for affected jobs. Root cause: an update to the broker's path-normalization util collapsed multiple path segments in some role ARNs, causing role lookup to return a truncated name which failed org-policy checks on target AWS accounts. Permanent fix: revert the faulty normalization logic and add unit/integration tests for multi-segment role ARNs; update broker to log the exact ARN used in STS requests for easier debugging.
